name: Spinal cord
summary: A cylinder of nervous tissue about 45 cm long in the adult, running from the foramen magnum to the conus medullaris at the L1–L2 disc, enclosed by the three meninges inside the vertebral canal. Its central H-shaped gray matter contains the motor neurons, sensory relay neurons and autonomic neurons of 31 segments; the surrounding white matter carries the long tracts in three funiculi. Two rules make cord lesions localizable: tracts have a fixed cross-sectional position (motor lateral, pain anterolateral, proprioception posterior), and the sensory level and reflex pattern mark the segment. Because the cord ends at L1–L2, lumbar puncture below L3 is safe and cauda equina lesions below the conus are lower motor neuron lesions.

anatomy.location: Vertebral canal from the cervicomedullary junction at the foramen magnum to the conus medullaris at the lower border of L1 (range T12–L3), with cervical and lumbosacral enlargements for the limbs, suspended by the denticulate ligaments and anchored below by the filum terminale; the cord segments lie progressively higher than the vertebrae of the same number.

subdivisions.name: Gray matter
subdivisions.note: anterior horn (motor), posterior horn (sensory), lateral horn T1–L2 (sympathetic) and S2–S4 (parasympathetic), central canal

subdivisions.name: White matter
subdivisions.note: posterior, lateral and anterior funiculi carrying the ascending and descending tracts

subdivisions.name: Segments
subdivisions.note: 8 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 5 sacral, 1 coccygeal, each with a pair of roots

subdivisions.name: Enlargements
subdivisions.note: cervical C5–T1 for the arm, lumbosacral L2–S3 for the leg

relations.anterior: vertebral bodies, posterior longitudinal ligament, discs
relations.lateral: pedicles and intervertebral foramina with the roots

function: Conducts all sensory information from the body to the brain and all motor commands from the brain to the body, and contains the segmental reflex circuits (stretch, withdrawal), the central pattern generators for locomotion and the autonomic outflow for the trunk, limbs, bladder, bowel and sexual function.

bestView.label: cervicomedullary junction and upper cervical cord (the only part within the MNI volume)

imaging.normalAppearance: The upper cervical cord is in the MNI volume; the rest needs a dedicated spine MRI. Sagittal T2 shows the cord as intermediate signal within bright CSF; axial T2 at 3 T shows the butterfly of gray matter. Cord signal change, swelling, atrophy, compression and the level of a lesion relative to the vertebrae are the key observations. Below the foramen magnum this atlas shows a curved reformat of the open PAM50 template (De Leener 2018), which images the brainstem and the whole cord at 0.5 mm but stores the cord straightened: its 475 mm of cord is resampled along the arc length of the atlas's own curved cord surface, so the brain MRI continues into a cord MRI in the same millimetre frame. It is a template average, so it shows the normal cord, the surrounding CSF and the vertebral levels but no individual variation, and its gray-matter butterfly is faint. The openly shareable edition may not redistribute PAM50, so below the foramen magnum it shows an average built here from openly licensed scans instead: ten spine-generic T2 volumes (0.8 mm isotropic, with manually labeled discs and nerve rootlets) for the cervical and upper thoracic cord, handing over to fourteen whole-spine sagittal T2 volumes of the Fudan lumbosacral dataset (0.6 mm in plane, 3.3 mm slices) for the rest of the cord, the conus and the lumbosacral sac. Each subject was straightened along its own cord, level-matched on its intervertebral discs and averaged, so vertebral levels are group means; spinal levels are measured on the rootlets only from C2 to T1 and follow the classical vertebral rule below that, which the readout marks.

pathology.pathology: Spinal cord compression (metastasis, disc, epidural abscess)
pathology.finding: Extradural mass displacing and flattening the cord with T2 signal change in the compressed segment; an emergency.
T2-bright intramedullary lesion: short (under 2 segments, peripheral) in MS, long (3 or more segments, central, swollen) in neuromyelitis optica and other longitudinally extensive myelitis.
Anterior two-thirds T2 hyperintensity with owl's eye anterior horns on axial images and restricted diffusion.
Central CSF-signal cavity within the cord, often with a Chiari malformation.
Inverted V T2 hyperintensity of the posterior columns over several cervical segments.

imaging.sequenceOfChoice: Sagittal and axial T2 with T1 and contrast; DWI for infarct; CT for bone

lesionEffects.deficit: Weakness below the level with upper motor neuron signs, lower motor neuron signs at the level
lesionEffects.mechanism: Descending tracts interrupted and anterior horn cells destroyed at the segment
Ascending tracts interrupted; the level is one to two segments below the lesion for spinothalamic modalities

lesionEffects.deficit: Spinal shock: flaccidity and areflexia after acute complete lesions
lesionEffects.mechanism: Transient loss of segmental excitability below the lesion

lesionEffects.deficit: Autonomic dysreflexia and orthostatic hypotension in lesions above T6
lesionEffects.mechanism: Loss of supraspinal control of the sympathetic outflow

examination: Sensory level to pin-prick and vibration, checked front and back
Power by myotome and the pattern of reflexes: absent at the level, brisk below
Anal tone, perianal sensation, bladder scan
Look for a Lhermitte sign, spinal tenderness and a girdle pain
pearls: Bilateral limb signs with a sensory level and sphincter disturbance and a normal face is the spinal cord
Spinal cord compression is the neurological emergency where hours matter: image the whole spine the same day
The sensory level on the trunk marks the lesion; the cord segment lies about one vertebra higher in the cervical region and two in the thoracic

pitfalls: A normal cervical MRI does not exclude a thoracic lesion; image the whole cord when the level is unclear
Early cord compression can present with pain alone
